faq.q: What is the entry post of the BCS Police cadre?
faq.a: Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) at Grade 9. It is the highest entry rank in Bangladesh Police, and officers join as probationers who first complete basic training at the Police Academy in Sardah.

faq.q: What is the salary of a BCS Police officer?

body_md:
**By [Daloyar Hassan Shishir](https://www.dhshishir.com)** · Career consultant, founder of Career Solutions and HereWeGrow · Facts last checked: 19 November 2026 · Last updated: 19 November 2026

> **Quick answer:** BCS (Police) is the cadre that supplies the leadership of Bangladesh Police. New officers join as Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) at Grade 9, the highest entry rank in the force, after a year-long basic course at the Bangladesh Police Academy in Sardah, Rajshahi. Under the new 9th pay scale the Grade 9 basic pay is listed at BDT 44,000, phased in up to July 2027. The 50th BCS advertised 117 Police cadre posts out of 1,755 cadre posts, and 290,951 people applied, so competition is very high. The ladder runs from ASP to Additional SP, SP, Additional DIG, DIG, Additional IGP and Inspector General of Police (IGP).

## Key facts (as of 19 November 2026)

| Question | Answer | Source type |
|---|---|---|
| What is the entry post? | Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP), probationer | Daily Star; Bangladesh Police portal |
| Entry grade | Grade 9 | Asia News Network (police grade table) |
| Starting basic pay | BDT 44,000 (new 9th scale, phased in to July 2027); old scale BDT 22,000 | Daily Star Bangla; teacher-portal summary |
| Police posts in the 50th BCS | 117 of 1,755 cadre posts | bdnews24; Rising BD |
| Applicants in the 50th BCS | 290,951 | Dhaka Times; Ittefaq |
| Basic training | 12 months at Bangladesh Police Academy, Sardah, then about 6 months of district practical training | Wikipedia; Bangladesh Police portal |
| Minimum height and weight (47th BCS circular) | Men 162.56 cm and 54.54 kg; women 152.40 cm and 45.45 kg | Prothom Alo |
| Exam | Preliminary 200 MCQ, written 900, viva 100 | BPSC |
| Who recruits | BPSC (cadre officers); Home Ministry's Public Security Division posts them | Daily Star |

*Numbers can change with each circular. The BPSC circular and the gazette are the final authority.*

## What does a BCS Police officer do?

A BCS Police officer leads, plans and supervises policing rather than walking a beat. After basic training, ASPs are posted to districts, circles and units, then rise to command police stations' supervisors, district forces, metropolitan units and specialised branches.

- **Law and order and crime control.** Supervising investigation of serious crimes, managing public order during events and elections, and coordinating with magistrates and prosecutors.
- **Specialised units.** Reports on police promotions and postings name the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), Special Branch, Highway Police, Police Telecom, the National Security Intelligence (NSI) and the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) as places where cadre officers serve.
- **Metropolitan policing.** In metropolitan forces such as Dhaka or Rajshahi, officers serve as Assistant Commissioner and rise through Deputy Commissioner and Additional Commissioner to Commissioner of Police.
- **Training and policy.** Senior officers train others at the Police Academy and Police Staff College and shape policy at Police Headquarters.

Two-thirds of ASP posts are filled directly through BCS, and the other third by promoting inspectors, according to a Daily Star explainer. That means the BCS route is the main door, not the only one.

## How is the career ladder structured?

| Rank | Pay grade | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) | 9 | Entry rank for BCS Police |
| Additional Superintendent of Police | 6 | Reported as Grade 6 in a Sept 2025 promotion of 59 ASPs |
| Superintendent of Police (SP) | 5 | Usually commands a district |
| Additional DIG | 4 | |
| Deputy Inspector General (DIG) | 3 | Range or unit command |
| Additional IGP | 2 (a few posts at Grade 1) | Senior Police Headquarters posts |
| Inspector General of Police (IGP) | 1 | Head of Bangladesh Police |

*A simplified map. The sanctioned posts at each grade have been reported as one IGP, two Additional IGP at Grade 1, 20 at Grade 2, 87 DIG, 201 Additional DIG, 596 SP and 1,008 Additional SP, but numbers change as the government creates or removes posts.*

**Promotion facts to know:**

- Promotions from ASP to SP are reviewed by a Departmental Promotion Committee headed by the secretary of the relevant ministry, according to a Jago News report. Promotions from Additional DIG to Additional IGP go through the Superior Selection Board, headed by the Cabinet Secretary.
- Merit, service record and any allegations of misconduct can affect promotion, as officers told Jago News.
- Reports describe long waits at some ranks and the use of supernumerary posts to promote officers where regular posts are not free. Do not assume the timeline in the rules will match real life.

## How many Police cadre posts are there, and how hard is it?

| Exam | Police posts | Total cadre posts |
|---|---|---|
| 50th BCS (circular Nov 2025) | 117 | 1,755 |

**Visual: share of cadre posts in the 50th BCS**

| Cadre | Posts | Visual |
|---|---|---|
| Health | 650 | █████████████████████████ |
| Administration | 200 | ████████ |
| Education | 185 | ███████ |
| Police | 117 | ████ |

In the 50th BCS, 290,951 people applied for the preliminary, 12,385 passed it, and 6,165 passed the written exam (result published 23 July 2026). For Police alone, 117 posts against 290,951 applicants is about one post for every 2,490 applicants, although candidates compete across many cadres and many will rank other cadres first. Allocation depends on your merit position, your cadre choices and the vacancies.

## What are the physical and medical standards?

The BCS circular sets minimum height and weight for the Police and Ansar cadres. In the 47th BCS circular reported by Prothom Alo, the minimum for men was 162.56 cm and 54.54 kg, and for women 152.40 cm and 45.45 kg. The application form asks you to enter height, weight and chest measurements.

- Check the 52nd BCS circular for the current numbers, because they can change.
- Medical boards are run by government hospitals for the cadres. Police Headquarters has asked for taller officers and for medical tests at the Central Police Hospital, so the rules may be reviewed.
- Start fitness work early. Basic training is physical as well as academic.

## What happens in training?

- **Basic course.** A 12-month ASP (probationary) course at the Bangladesh Police Academy in Sardah, Rajshahi, according to the academy's course table on Wikipedia. The academy's Police portal describes law, physical training, driving, computer and equestrian skills and musketry.
- **Practical training.** After the course, probationers spend about six months in a district, split between a police station, a circle and other offices.
- **Discipline is strict.** Six probationary ASPs of the 41st BCS were dismissed during training, and six of the 40th BCS were dismissed in 2024, according to The Financial Express and Dhaka Tribune. Show-cause notices were also issued to 25 trainees of the 40th batch for disrupting training.
- **No full pay during some police training.** Cadet sub-inspectors, who are a different group, receive no salary during basic training. Check your own terms in your appointment letter.

## What is the salary and what are the benefits?

The 9th National Pay Scale was approved by cabinet on 31 August 2026 and takes effect from 1 July 2026. Basic pay is raised in stages up to July 2027, so early pay is below the final figure. Allowances are reset from January 2028.

| Rank | Grade | Old basic (BDT) | New basic (BDT) |
|---|---|---|---|
| ASP | 9 | 22,000 | 44,000 |
| Additional SP | 6 | 35,500 | 71,000 |
| SP | 5 | 43,000 | 86,000 |
| DIG | 3 | 56,500 | 1,13,000 |
| Additional IGP | 2 | 66,000 | 1,32,000 |
| IGP | 1 | 78,000 | 1,56,000 |

*Source note: these figures come from a teacher-portal summary of the new scale, not the gazette. The Daily Star Bangla separately confirms Grade 1 at BDT 1,56,000. Always check the gazette before you quote a figure.*

**Benefits beyond basic pay** (check your appointment terms): house rent and medical allowance, festival bonuses, leave and pension under government service rules, uniform and official support, and training in Bangladesh and abroad. Policing also brings long hours, night duty and risk. Count those honestly before you rank this cadre first.

## Which skills does a Police officer need?

| Skill | Why it matters | Demand |
|---|---|---|
| Criminal law and procedure | Penal Code, Code of Criminal Procedure, evidence | █████ |
| Investigation oversight | Supervising evidence, interviews, case files | █████ |
| Physical fitness and discipline | Basic training and field duty | █████ |
| Integrity and resisting pressure | Public trust and legal risk | █████ |
| Leadership under stress | Commanding teams in a crisis | ████ |
| Communication and de-escalation | Crowds, victims, media | ████ |
| Crisis and event management | Elections, disasters, public events | ███ |
| Digital and cyber literacy | Cybercrime and digital evidence | ███ |
| Official writing | Reports and case notes | ███ |

*Bars show our reading of the role, not a survey.*

## How do I get in? The exam path

Police uses the general BCS exam: a 200-mark MCQ preliminary, a 900-mark written exam (Bangla 200, English 200, Bangladesh Affairs 200, International Affairs 100, Mathematical Reasoning and Mental Ability 100, General Science and Technology 100) and a 100-mark viva. See our BCS overview for the full guide.

**To aim for Police:**

1. Put Police on your cadre choice list only if you truly want the work, with realistic second and third choices.
2. Check the height and weight rules before you apply. Do not rely on rumours.
3. Build writing speed early. The written exam decides most of the rank.
4. Study criminal law basics, human rights and the Constitution. They help in the viva.
5. Prepare viva answers about discipline, ethics and your own district's crime and safety issues.
6. Keep a plan B.

## Where will you find more peace of mind?

No cadre is free of pressure, and we have no survey to rank them. Police work involves shifts, emergencies, public anger and political pressure. Reports of delayed promotion and officers kept without a post also show how senior careers can depend on circumstances. Three habits protect your peace: clean, documented decisions, a firm boundary between work and family time, and a few honest colleagues and mentors outside your chain of command.

## Plan your own path (5-minute worksheet)

Copy these lines and fill them in today:

1. **My age on the next cut-off date:** ___ (must be 32 or under)
2. **My height and weight against the circular:** ___ cm, ___ kg
3. **My cadre choices:** 1) Police 2) ___ 3) ___
4. **Three weakest subjects:** ___, ___, ___
5. **My weekly fitness routine:** ___
6. **My plan B if I do not get a cadre:** ___

Then take the free skill test on this page and compare the result with line 4.

## Faith and history: the trust of power

**The Quran.** Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:8 tells believers to stand firm for God and be just, and not to let hatred of a people lead them away from justice ([read it on quran.com](https://quran.com/5/8)). A police officer holds the power to restrain, and this verse sets the standard for using it.

**Hadith.** The Prophet (peace be upon him) said that each of you is a shepherd and each is responsible for his flock (Sahih al-Bukhari 893; Sahih Muslim 1829). A police officer's flock is every person in the area, including the weak and the accused.

**History.** The Bangladesh Police Academy at Sardah began in 1912 as a police training college serving Bengal and Assam and was raised to a national police academy in the 1960s, according to the Bangladesh Police portal and Wikipedia.

## Your contribution to the nation

A well-led police force protects a girl on her way to school, a trader's shop at night and a voter in a queue. An ASP who makes sure cases are recorded, evidence is kept and complaints are heard fairly builds the trust that lets citizens use the law instead of fear. Honest leadership at this level shapes how the whole force behaves.

## Your contribution to the world

Police officers learn crisis command, investigation oversight and community policing. Many serve in international peacekeeping contexts or study criminology, security and human rights abroad. Skills in evidence-based policing, cybercrime and disaster response are valued by international bodies. Check current opportunities through Police Headquarters and the Ministry of Home Affairs.

## If you do not get BCS Police

- **Other BCS cadres.** The same exam leads to Administration, Foreign Affairs, Taxation, Customs, Audit and more.
- **Sub-Inspector (SI) route.** Bangladesh Police recruits sub-inspectors directly as a non-cadre entry, with a graduation requirement, according to The Daily Star. Check current circulars.
- **Sergeant and other uniformed roles**, and other security and law enforcement agencies.
- **Law, security and risk jobs in the private and development sectors.**

## Research opportunities

- Topics with real need: police-community relations, cybercrime investigation, crowd management, women in policing, police training methods, promotion and cadre policy.
- Where to learn: criminology, law and public administration departments, the Police Staff College and policy think tanks.
- Path: a strong master's thesis, a research assistant post, then MPhil or PhD.

## Whom to follow and learn from

Follow institutions: [BPSC](https://www.bpsc.gov.bd), [Bangladesh Police](https://police.portal.gov.bd), the [Police Academy](https://bpa.police.gov.bd) and the Ministry of Home Affairs. Treat coaching centre promises and social media rank claims with caution.

## Where do I find circulars?

- BPSC's official site: [bpsc.gov.bd](https://www.bpsc.gov.bd).
- Teletalk's BPSC application portal: bpsc.teletalk.com.bd.
- Daily newspapers' job pages (cross-check every date and number with the circular).

**No lobbying.** Tadbir during the application process is treated as grounds for disqualification.

## How should I write my profile and CV?

BCS does not choose candidates from a CV. Marks decide. A short, honest profile helps in the viva and in backup applications.

| Weak line | Better line |
|---|---|
| Fit and disciplined. | Completed 3 years of university sports training and led a 15-member volunteer safety team at campus events. |
| Wants to serve the nation. | Volunteered 100 hours with a community safety group and wrote a short report on local road accidents. |
| Good communicator. | Moderated 8 student debates and handled complaints at a union digital centre. |

*Use only real, provable figures.*

Build yours free with the HereWeGrow CV Builder.

## What are the common mistakes?

- Choosing Police for status without understanding the hours, risk and pressure.
- Ignoring the height and weight rules until the medical board.
- Skipping written practice because "marks are in viva".
- Giving textbook answers in the viva instead of your own examples.
- Having no plan B.
- Believing rumours about marks or posts instead of the circular.

## Changelog

- **19 Nov 2026:** First version. Facts checked against the sources listed below. Post numbers from the 50th BCS; physical standards from the 47th BCS circular as reported by Prothom Alo.
- Next planned review: when the 52nd BCS circular is published.

cover_letter_md:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the [position] advertised on [site/date]. I hold a [degree] from [university] and have strong Bangla and English writing, discipline and people-management skills built while preparing for the BCS Police cadre. In [project/volunteering role] I [one provable result, e.g. led a 15-member team that managed safety at a campus event with no incident].

My CV is attached as a PDF. I would be glad to attend an interview.

Sincerely,
[Your name] | [Phone] | [Email]

(Note: BCS itself needs no cover letter. Use this for backup non-BCS applications.)
interview_qs: Why do you want to join the Police cadre? (Tip: Give a real reason from experience; talk about protecting people, not power or status.)
What does an ASP do in the first years? (Tip: Mention training at Sardah, district practical training and supervision duties.)
What would you do if a powerful person pressured you to drop a case? (Tip: Follow the law, document the request, inform your superior, stay polite.)
How would you handle a violent crowd outside a police station? (Tip: Safety first, communicate, use minimum necessary force, coordinate with magistrates, and record decisions.)
How would you treat a complainant who is poor and not well spoken? (Tip: Listen fully, record the complaint properly, and explain next steps.)
What is the difference between an arrest and a detention? How do rights apply? (Tip: Stay within basics you know; mention the Constitution and legal safeguards.)
How do you stay fit and disciplined? (Tip: Give a real weekly routine with numbers.)
Tell us about your district and its main safety problems. (Tip: Two facts, two problems, one realistic solution.)
How should police handle cybercrime and online harassment? (Tip: Evidence preservation, victim support, cooperation with specialist units.)
What is community policing? (Tip: Partnership with residents; one practical example.)
Why not Administration or another cadre? (Tip: Show you know the other cadre; explain your fit with Police.)
How do you handle stress and long, irregular hours? (Tip: Share a real habit: sleep, exercise, talking to a mentor.)
Describe a time you led or organised people. (Tip: Situation, action, result in numbers if possible.)
What will you do if you are not selected this time? (Tip: Show a calm plan B; do not sound defeated.)
Do you have any questions for us? (Tip: Ask about training or learning, not about pay or posting.)
